questions.q:
Match the List-I with List-II:

List I List II
A Microwaves I Radioactive decay of the nucleus
B Gamma rays II Rapid acceleration and deceleration of electron in aerials
C Radio waves III Inner shell electrons
D X-rays IV Klystron valve

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A)& A Klystron valve or the magnetron valve are generally used for the production of electromagnetic waves and that electromagnetic wave is Microwave. So,& \left(A\right) \to IV$.

(B)~Gamma rays are produced during the disintegration of radioactive atomic nuclei and the decay of certain subatomic particles.So,~\left(B\right) \to I$

(C)~Radio waves can be produced by rapid acceleration and deceleration of electrons in aerials (conductors). These can be detected by receivers of aerials.~So,~\left(C\right) \to II$

(D)~X-rays are produced when a metal target or any other element is bombarded with high energy particles such as electrons, photons or ions. When high energy electrons is incident on a bound electron in an atom, then bound electron emits from the inner shell of that atom.~So,~\left(D\right) \to III$

questions.q: The waves emitted when a metal target is bombarded with high energy electrons are
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: The bombarding electrons can eject electrons from the inner shells of the atoms of the metal target.& Those vacancies will be quickly filled by electrons dropping from higher levels, emitting x-rays with sharply defined frequencies associated with the difference between the atomic energy levels of the target atoms. Hence, X-rays are emitted when a metal target is bombarded with high energy electrons.&

questions.q: There are two infinitely long straight current-carrying conductors and they are held at right angles to each other so that their common ends meet at the origin as shown in the figure given below. The ratio of current in both conductors is $1: 1$.~The magnetic field at point $P$ is_________ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pi y} \left(1 + sin{θ}_{1}\right) + $\dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pi x}\left($1 + sin{θ}_{2}\right)$
$B = $\dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pi y}\left($1 + $\dfrac{x}{x^{2} + y^{2}}\right) + \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pi x} \left(1 + $\dfrac{y}{x^{2} + y^{2}}\right)

$B = $\dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pi x} + \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pi y} + \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pi} \left[\dfrac{x}{y\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}} + \dfrac{y}{x\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}}\right]$⇒ B = $\dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pi}\left[\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{y}\right] + \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pi}\dfrac{x^{2} + y^{2}}{xy} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pi} \left[\dfrac{x + y + \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}}{xy}\right]$

$$

$\mathrm{E}=\sqrt{\left(\mathrm{E}_0\right)^2+\left(\mathrm{E}_0\right)^2+2\left(\mathrm{E}_0\right)\left(\mathrm{E}_0\right) \cos \frac{\pi}{3}}$

questions.q:
Match List I and List II

A Gauss’s Law in& Electrostatics I $∮ \overset{→}{E} \cdot \overset{→}{dl} = - \dfrac{d{ϕ}_{B}}{dt}$
B Faraday's Law II $∮ \overset{→}{B} \cdot d\overset{→}{A} = 0$~
C Gauss’s Law in Magnetism III $∮ \overset{→}{B} \cdot d\overset{→}{l} = {μ}_{0}{i}_ + {μ}_{0}{∈}_{0}\dfrac{d{ϕ}_{E}}{dt}$
D Ampere-Maxwell Law IV $∮ \overset{→}{E} \cdot d\overset{→}{s} = \dfrac{q}{\in 0}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A) Gauss law states that the total electric flux out of a closed surface is equal to the charge enclosed divided by the permittivity. So,& $ϕ = ∮ \overset{→}{E} \cdot d\overset{→}{s} = \dfrac{q}{\in 0}$

(B) Faraday’s law~explains that the direction of the current will be opposite to the direction of flux that produced it, so~$∮ \overset{→}{E} \cdot d\overset{→}{l} = - \dfrac{d{ϕ}_{B}}{dt}$

(C) Gauss's law for magnetism states that the magnetic flux B across any closed surface is zero, so~$∮ \overset{→}{B} \cdot d\overset{→}{A} = 0$

(D) Ampere’s Maxwell law is stated as~

$∮ \overset{→}{B} \cdot d\overset{→}{l} = {μ}_{0}{i}_{c} + {μ}_{0}{∈}_{0}\dfrac{d{ϕ}_{E}}{dt}$

Where~${i}_{c} =$Conduction current and~

${∈}_{0}\dfrac{d{ϕ}_{E}}{dt} =$Displacement current

Thus,& A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

!

questions.q: An electric bulb is rated as $200W$. What will be the peak magnetic field at $4m$ distance produced by the radiations coming from this bulb? Consider this bulb as a point source with $3 . 5 %$ efficiency.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Intensity of light is& $I = \dfrac{Power}{Area} = \dfrac{200 \times \dfrac{3 . 5}{100}}{4\pi\left(4\right)2} = 0 . 034Wm^{- 2}$

Using the relation between magnetic field and intensity,~$I = \dfrac{{B}_{0}^{2}c}{2{μ}_{0}}$

We have, magnetic field as~${B}_{0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{I \times 2{μ}_{0}}{c}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{0 . 034 \times 2 \times 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}}{3 \times {10}^{8}}} = 1 . 69 \times {10}^{- 8}T \approx 1 . 71 \times {10}^{- 8}T$

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave of frequency $5GHz$, is travelling in a medium whose relative electric permittivity and relative magnetic permeability both are $2 .$ Its velocity in this medium is _______\times {10}^{7}ms^{- 1}.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given : Frequency of wave $f = 5GHz$

$= 5 \times {10}^{9}Hz$

Relative permittivity, ${ϵ}_{r} = 2$~and Relative permeability, ${μ}_{r} = 2$~Since speed of light in a medium is given by,

$v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu} \in} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{μ}_{r}{μ}_{0} \cdot {ϵ}_{r}{∈}_{0}}}$

$v = \dfrac{1}{{μ}_{r}{ϵ}_{f}}\dfrac{1}{{μ}_{0}{ϵ}_{0}} = \dfrac{C}{{μ}_{r}{ϵ}_{r}}$

Where $C$ is speed of light is vacuum

$∴ v = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}}{\sqrt{4}} = \dfrac{30 \times {10}^{7}}{2}ms^{- 1}$

$= 15 \times {10}^{7}ms^{- 1}$

$∴$ Ans. is $15$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{hc}{λ} = mc^{2}$

$⇒ m = \dfrac{h}{c\lambda} = \dfrac{h}{3 \times {10}^{8} \times 10 \times {10}^{- 10}} = \dfrac{10h}{3}kg$

questions.q:
The intensity of the light from a bulb incident on a surface is $0 . 22Wm^{- 2}$. The amplitude of the magnetic field in this light-wave is _____~$\times {10}^{- 9}T$

(Given : Permittivity of vacuum ${ϵ}_{0} = 8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 12}C^{2}N^{- 1}m^{- 2}$, speed of light in vacuum $c = 3 \times {10}^{8}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The intensity is defined as energy per unit time per unit area. Therefore,& $I = \dfrac{dE}{Adt}$.

Energy density is energy per unit volume. Therefore,~${U}_{d} = \dfrac{dE}{Adx}$.

Dividing $\dfrac{I}{Ud} = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = c$

$⇒ {U}_{d} = \dfrac{I}{c} = \dfrac{0 . 22}{3 \times {10}^{8}} = \dfrac{22}{3} \times {10}^{- 10}Jm^{- 3}$

Magnetic energy density will be half of total energy density, Therefore,~${U}_{b} = \dfrac{11}{3} \times {10}^{- 10}Jm^{- 3}$.

Now energy density in magnetic field is given by,~${U}_{b} = \dfrac{B2}{2{μ}_{0}}$. Therefore,

${B}_{rms}^{2}2{μ}_{0} = \dfrac{11}{3} \times {10}^{- 10}Jm^{- 3}$ where ${B}_{rms}^{2} = \left(\dfrac{B0}{2}\right) = {B}_{0}^{2}2$

$⇒ {B}_{0}^{2}4{μ}_{0} = \dfrac{11}{3} \times {10}^{- 10} ⇒ {B}_{0} = \sqrt{4 \times \left(4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}\right) \times \dfrac{11}{3} \times {10}^{- 10}} ⇒ {B}_{0} = 4 . 29 \times {10}^{- 8}T ≃ 43 \times {10}^{- 9}T$
